description: One action by its id: its inputs, what it gives and its price rule. With arguments (the person's real inputs) it also prices that exact run: the most it can cost, what it usually costs, the balance, and a consent sentence to read to the person. Nothing runs and nothing is charged. With rows or rows_text (up to 100, for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website) it prices a whole list. Use it before every paid run. For builders: endpoint_ids or exclude_endpoint_ids add the provider list those take. Free. NOT for: finding the id, which is capability_search, or running, which is run_capability.

arguments.description: Optional: the run's inputs, by name, to price that exact run (a quote only; nothing runs).

endpoint_ids.description: With arguments: price the run on these providers only (endpoint ids from this answer).

exclude_endpoint_ids.description: With arguments: price the run without these providers.

id.description: An action id or tool id from capability_search.

max_items.description: With arguments: most rows to price for, 1-100. Default 10.

rows.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. One object per row, such as {"name": "Jane Doe", "domain": "example.com"} or {"name": "Example Ltd", "country": "GB"}.

rows_text.description: A list for people.email.find or companies.register.search or companies.emails.from_website: 1 to 100 rows, each run once as its own run with its own exact cost. Instead of rows: paste up to 100 rows as text, one per line ("Jane Doe, example.com"; "Example Ltd, GB") or a CSV with a header row (name, domain, linkedin_url; name, country).

timeout_seconds.description: With arguments: longest the run may take, 1-180 seconds. Default: the provider's own (60, more for slow sources).

name: capability_inspect
title: Read and price an action
